To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a bio-inspired approach to the reconstruction of nearly extinct software systems.
we propose and implement a novel bio-inspired approach for reconstruction of complex software systems from a state of near extinction, and we evaluate our approach on a real case study.

1) a co-DNA is a computational analogue of DNA and can be encoded as a string of characters; 2) a system can be reconstructed by encoding a co-DNA of the system and using it for transforming computational devices into system cells; 3) system cells can spread the co-DNA and reconstruct the system; 4) the reconstruction of a system can be performed in a decentralized manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational analogues of the biological processes of DNA transcription, replication and translation.
the development of computational DNA, computational analogues of genetic processes, and a co-DNA based approach for reconstructing a software system in the absence of human intervention.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the approach is able to reconstruct a software system in a way that is similar to the biological processes that take place during the evolution of a biological system, i.e., it is able to reconstruct the software system by spreading the system reconstruction over computational devices.
the co-DNA approach can be considered a viable alternative for the reconstruction of complex software systems from near extinct states.
our approach is a novel and promising way of enabling software systems to reconstruct themselves in a distributed manner from a state of near-extinction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have introduced an approach for the reconstruction of nearly extinct software systems that is based on the encoding of their functionality as a co-DNA and the transformation of the computational devices in which the system was deployed into system cells that execute chunks of the system’s functionality and spread further the reconstruction process.

the proposed approach is a novel bio-inspired approach for the reconstruction of nearly extinct systems, where a computational DNA of a system is encoded and then transmitted through a network of computational devices, and then used to transform these devices into system components that realise chunks of the systems functionality and spread further the reconstruction process.
we are proposing a bio-inspired approach that enables the transmission of the computational DNA of a system, which in turn enables the reconstruction of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a bio-inspired approach can provide an alternative solution for reconstructing complex software systems in case of extensive damage, and it may also be used as a complementary solution to other existing approaches.
the bio-inspired approach is able to recover a complex system functionality from a state of near extinction.

, through the co-DNA, we provide a way for reconstructing a system from a nearly extinct state by using a set of computational devices that may not have been designed for the original system, and without the need for any human intervention.
